plans.name: WHO healthy diet
plans.summary: Limits on fat, saturated fat and sodium; at least 25 g of fibre and 3,510 mg of potassium a day.

sources.title: Healthy diet, fact sheet of 26 January 2026
Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIV: the energy in a gram of fat, protein and carbohydrate, used here to turn grams into a share of energy

checks.label: Fat, share of energy
checks.basis: WHO: total fat 30% or less of total daily energy

checks.label: Saturated fat, share of energy
checks.basis: WHO: no more than 10% of total energy from saturated fat

checks.label: Carbohydrate, share of energy
checks.basis: WHO: approximately 45–75% of total daily energy

checks.label: Protein, share of energy
checks.basis: WHO: 10–15% of total daily energy is generally sufficient for adults

checks.label: Fibre
checks.basis: WHO: at least 25 g of naturally occurring dietary fibre a day

checks.label: Sodium
checks.basis: WHO: less than 5 g of salt a day (2 g of sodium)

checks.label: Potassium
checks.basis: WHO: at least 3,510 mg a day may be beneficial for adults

unmeasured: Free sugars under 10% of energy: the food tables give total sugars, and cannot tell free sugars from the rest.
At least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day: the food tables do not say which foods are fruit or vegetables.
No more than 1% of energy from trans fat: the food list carries no trans fat value.

plans.name: European reference values
plans.summary: EFSA's adult reference intakes for protein, fat, carbohydrate, fibre and the main minerals and vitamins.

sources.title: Dietary reference values for nutrients, summary report (2017); sodium 2019
Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIV: the energy in a gram of fat, protein and carbohydrate

checks.label: Protein
checks.basis: EFSA: 0.83 g for each kg of body weight a day (population reference intake)

checks.label: Fat, share of energy
checks.basis: EFSA: 20–35% of energy (reference intake range)

checks.label: Carbohydrate, share of energy
checks.basis: EFSA: 45–60% of energy (reference intake range)

checks.label: Fibre
checks.basis: EFSA: 25 g a day (adequate intake)

checks.label: Sodium
checks.basis: EFSA 2019: 2.0 g a day is safe and adequate

checks.label: Potassium
checks.basis: EFSA: 3,500 mg a day (adequate intake)

checks.label: Calcium
checks.basis: EFSA: 950 mg a day, 1,000 mg at 18–24; upper level 2,500 mg

checks.label: Iron
checks.basis: EFSA: 11 mg a day for men; 16 mg for women before the menopause, 11 mg after

checks.label: Magnesium
checks.basis: EFSA: 350 mg a day for men, 300 mg for women (adequate intake)

checks.label: Vitamin C
checks.basis: EFSA: 110 mg a day for men, 95 mg for women

checks.label: Vitamin D
checks.basis: EFSA: 15 µg a day (adequate intake); upper level 100 µg

checks.label: Vitamin B12
checks.basis: EFSA: 4.0 µg a day (adequate intake)

checks.label: Folate
checks.basis: EFSA: 330 µg of dietary folate equivalents a day

unmeasured: Saturated fat: EFSA says “as low as possible” and gives no number, so nothing is measured for it here.
Vitamin A: EFSA counts retinol equivalents, which the food list does not store.

plans.name: Energy and protein for me
plans.summary: A daily energy estimate from your sex, age, height, weight and how active you are, and protein for your weight.

sources.title: Basal metabolic rate studies in humans. Public Health Nutrition 2005;8(7A):1133–52, Table 15: the equations EFSA adopted in 2013
Activity levels of 1.4, 1.6, 1.8 and 2.0 for low active, moderately active, active and very active lifestyles — “a rough indication”

sources.by: WHO, FAO and UNU (2007); European Food Safety Authority
sources.title: Protein: 0.83 g for each kg of body weight a day

checks.label: Energy
checks.basis: Henry’s equation for your sex and age, times EFSA’s activity level. An estimate: change it if it does not fit you.

checks.label: Protein
checks.basis: 0.83 g for each kg of body weight a day (WHO/FAO/UNU 2007; EFSA)

unmeasured: Whether the estimate is right for you: it is an average for people of your sex, age, size and activity, and says nothing about gaining or losing weight.

plans.name: Two fasting days a week
plans.summary: Two days a week on up to a quarter of your energy need. Defined by an international consensus; recommended by no public body found.

sources.title: International consensus on fasting terminology. Cell Metabolism 2024;36(8):1779–94 — “modified fasting”: “limiting energy intake to typically up to 25% of energy needs on modified fasting days”, for example “on 2 separate or consecutive days per week”

sources.by: Henry CJK; European Food Safety Authority
sources.title: The energy need the quarter is taken of: Henry’s equation times EFSA’s activity level

checks.label: Fasting days this week
checks.basis: A day counts when what you logged comes to a quarter of your energy need or less (Koppold et al. 2024)

unmeasured: A day you logged nothing on is not counted as a fasting day: formicaria cannot tell fasting from not writing it down.
plans.caution: This is a definition, not advice. The consensus says therapeutic fasting is individually tailored and medically supervised fasting is led by a trained physician.

plans.name: Alternate-day modified fasting
plans.summary: A day of eating freely, then a day on up to a quarter of your energy need. A definition, not a recommendation.

sources.title: International consensus on fasting terminology. Cell Metabolism 2024;36(8):1779–94 — alternate-day modified fasting: “alternating a day of eating ad libitum and a day of modified fasting”

sources.by: Henry CJK; European Food Safety Authority
sources.title: The energy need the quarter is taken of

checks.label: Fasting days this week
checks.basis: Every other day is three or four days of a week; a day counts at a quarter of your energy need or less

unmeasured: That the days alternate: formicaria counts them and does not check their order.
A day you logged nothing on is not counted as a fasting day.
plans.caution: This is a definition, not advice. The consensus says therapeutic fasting is individually tailored and medically supervised fasting is led by a trained physician.

plans.name: Time-restricted eating
plans.summary: All eating inside a part of the day, leaving at least 14 hours without. You say each day whether you kept to it.

sources.title: International consensus on fasting terminology. Cell Metabolism 2024;36(8):1779–94 — “a daily fasting window of at least 14 hours. There is no explicit limit on energy intake during eating hours”

checks.label: Days you kept to it this week
checks.basis: You say so each day: what you log has a day and no time of day, so formicaria cannot measure the hours

unmeasured: The hours themselves: a logged food has a day and no time.
plans.caution: This is a definition, not advice.

plans.name: Nordic recommendations 2023
plans.summary: Food-group amounts from the Nordic Nutrition Recommendations. You say each day whether you kept to them.

sources.title: Nordic Nutrition Recommendations 2023, Table 24

checks.label: Days you kept to it this week
checks.basis: You say so each day

describes: Vegetables, fruit and berries: 500–800 g a day
Whole grains: at least 90 g a day
Fish: 300–450 g a week, 200 g of it fatty
Red meat: at most 350 g a week
Vegetable oil: at least 25 g a day
unmeasured: All of it: no food table used here tells whole grain from refined, says which group a mixed dish belongs to, or marks dairy as low-fat.

plans.name: Planetary health diet
plans.summary: The EAT-Lancet Commission's daily food-group amounts for about 2,400 kcal. You say each day whether you kept to them.

sources.title: Summary report, 2025

checks.label: Days you kept to it this week
checks.basis: You say so each day

describes: Red meat: 15 g; poultry: 30 g; fish: 30 g; eggs: 15 g
unmeasured: All of it: the food tables do not sort foods into these groups.

plans.name: WHO weekly activity
plans.summary: At least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week, or 75 of vigorous, and muscle strengthening on 2 days.

sources.title: Guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour (2020), adults 18–64
Physical activity guidelines for adults aged 19 to 64: which activities count as what, and the talk test

checks.label: Activity this week
checks.basis: WHO: at least 150–300 min of moderate activity a week, or 75–150 of vigorous, or a mix. A vigorous minute counts as two.

checks.label: Strengthening days this week
checks.basis: WHO: muscle-strengthening activities involving all major muscle groups on 2 or more days a week

unmeasured: That strengthening reaches all major muscle groups: follow a strength regime here if you want that counted.
plans.caution: WHO has separate recommendations for pregnancy, chronic conditions and disability, which formicaria does not assess.

guides.label: Strength exercises to do at home

plans.name: WHO weekly activity, 65 and over
plans.summary: The same weekly activity, with balance and strength work on 3 or more days.

sources.title: Guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour (2020), adults 65 and over

checks.label: Activity this week
checks.basis: WHO: at least 150–300 min of moderate activity a week, or 75–150 of vigorous. A vigorous minute counts as two.

checks.label: Strengthening days this week
checks.basis: WHO: muscle strengthening on 2 or more days a week

checks.label: Balance days this week
checks.basis: WHO: varied multicomponent activity emphasising functional balance and strength on 3 or more days a week

plans.caution: UK Chief Medical Officers: with frailty, dementia, vertebral fractures or regular falls, new exercises may be better supervised by a trained professional at first.

plans.name: Falls prevention
plans.summary: Balance-challenging and functional exercise in 3 or more sessions a week, for at least 12 weeks.

sources.title: World guidelines for falls prevention and management for older adults (2022)

checks.label: Balance sessions this week
checks.basis: World Falls Guidelines: 3 or more sessions a week, individualised and progressed, for at least 12 weeks

unmeasured: That the exercise is individualised and progressed, which the guideline asks for.
plans.caution: The guideline expects this to be tailored to the person. Otago and similar named programmes are prescribed by a physiotherapist.

plans.name: Strength, twice a week
plans.summary: Every major muscle group at least twice a week, at least 2 sets an exercise, stopping short of failure.

sources.title: Currier et al., position stand on resistance training, Med Sci Sports Exerc 2026;58(4):851–72 (read from a copy of the paper)

checks.label: Each body region, days this week
checks.basis: ACSM 2026: “at least twice weekly, with all major muscle groups being engaged”. It names no muscles; formicaria counts four regions.

unmeasured: At least 2 sets an exercise, and stopping 2–3 repetitions short of failure: formicaria records the sets you do and not how hard each was.

guides.label: Strength exercises to do at home

plans.name: Muscle growth
plans.summary: Ten or more sets a week for each muscle group, at any load, on as many days as you like.

sources.title: Currier et al., position stand on resistance training, Med Sci Sports Exerc 2026;58(4):851–72, Table 6 (read from a copy of the paper)

checks.label: Lower body, pulling: sets this week
checks.basis: ACSM 2026: 10 or more sets a week per muscle group

plans.name: Minimal strength
plans.summary: Three exercises — legs, an upper-body pull, an upper-body push — and at least 4 sets a week for each.

sources.title: No time to lift? Designing time-efficient training programs for strength and hypertrophy: a narrative review. Sports Medicine 2021

checks.basis: Iversen et al. 2021: one upper-body pushing exercise
